findings.source_en: Baerand? Let me guess... the anger.
findings.issue: The glossary freezes 'Baer / Baerand' on a single approved form, باير, but the long form is rendered بايراند here (and in Greeting_02_10 and Greeting_04_10) while the short form is باير in Greeting_NoProof_13_10. Either the glossary row needs a second approved form for Baerand, or these rows must collapse to باير. Reporting only - needs an owner ruling, since collapsing them erases the short/long distinction Franz uses.

'hungers' rendered تتوق (yearns). Everywhere else in Franz's lines the forge's hunger is جائع/جوع (Interact_04_10 'She's hungerin' fiercely' -> جائعة بشدّة), so this row breaks the motif as well as softening it.

findings.source_en: Come on. Feed her. She’s starving!
findings.issue: 'starving' rendered جائعة, the same word used for plain 'hungry' two rows over. The intensity step is lost.

Franz's appraisal lines form a graded ladder (Amateur / Crude but it'll do / Acceptable / Good for a journeyman / competent / Fine work). 'It's… competent' and 'Fine work. Good even.' (Upgrade_13_10) both land on لا بأس به, so two different rungs read identically in game.

Ambiguous in isolation, resolved by real scene order (_10/_20/_30): 'Making anything worthwhile is [dangerous].' -> 'Your brother was too much for your mum.' -> 'At least he made it.' 'Made it' is survived - the brother lived, the mother did not. استطاع هو reads as 'at least he managed it', i.e. he succeeded at some task.
